front.title: Root Time Source Alignment Signature and Transport Protocol for NTPv5

abstract.t:
This document defines an NTPv5 extension that turns a time value's provenance from a _claim_ into _evidence_. A pre-trusted Root Time Source attests that a given time service instance's clock has been checked for alignment against a physical source; that instance then signs the time value itself. A client holding only the root public key verifies both signatures offline, so it can tell a time value that carries verifiable provenance apart from one that merely claims it.
The extension deliberately does one thing and no more: it proves _where a signed time value came from_. It does not adjust clocks, it does not rate sources, and it has no revocation -- a signed proof is unilateral, it exists once signed. It is opt-in, uses two extension fields, and touches nothing in the core protocol.
